clue.text: Look surprised — space programme's ending

parts.note: a gap is an empty space

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of programme

explanation.surface: Someone reacts with astonishment as a space programme comes to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare open-mouthed, the classic expression of astonishment.

clue.text: Reckon pub out of Irish beer?

indicators.note: one thing taken out of another leaves the remainder behind

parts.note: the famous Irish stout
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders whether the pub has run out of Guinness.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove INN from GUINNESS to leave GUESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to estimate or suppose, which is what a guess does.

clue.text: Well-known dog nursing rook in hospital department

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: short for Pomeranian, a small dog
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
taken as written
ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: A dog is being cared for in a hospital ward, oddly with a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: The rook is the chess piece, not the bird; ENT stands for ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prominent stands out and is widely recognised, hence famous or well-known.

clue.text: Up close and personal truth about drug of winner

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a fact is a truth
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written
an ace is a winning shot, as in tennis

explanation.surface: An intimate exposé reveals the truth about a champion's drug-taking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' is taken literally as part of the wordplay, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Face-to-face means in direct personal contact, the same intimacy as 'up close and personal'.

clue.text: Ideas revised about horned beast in Christian emblem?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap around the beast
revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder
a gnu is a horned African antelope

explanation.surface: Someone rethinks their ideas about a horned animal appearing as a religious symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: Agnus Dei is Latin for Lamb of God, a lamb shown carrying a cross or banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamb figure is used as a symbol of Christ; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Where City types hide cream cake …

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, where financiers work
a hide is a hiding place, as a lair is

explanation.surface: City workers sneak off to a hiding place with a cream cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb but is a noun, a place to hide. The ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger of choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: … getting an excess of it?

parts.note: surface reading: following on from the cream cake, someone gets too much of 'it', cream
setter's reading: 'it' is the old slang for sex, so the clue describes a person with too much of that

explanation.surface: After the cream cake, someone ends up with far too much of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the cake clue, so 'it' seems to be cream; but 'it' is a familiar euphemism for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone oversexed has an excessive sexual appetite, literally too much 'it'.

clue.text: Peculiar charm found in Gesta Romanorum

indicators.note: something found in a phrase is sitting inside its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A medieval Latin story collection, the Gesta Romanorum, has a peculiar charm.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma, figuratively, is a distinctive atmosphere or quality attached to something.

clue.text: Long poem complete? One's omitted most intense part!

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem

indicators.note: something omitted is left out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: entire means complete
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A critic asks whether a long poem is finished, noting that one key passage is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: ENTIRE loses its I to become ENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point above an earthquake's origin, and by extension the focal centre of any activity.

clue.text: This writer's rich source

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to the setter, 'this writer' being me
second meaning: an abundant supply, as of gold or information

explanation.surface: An author boasts that their own work is a rich source.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for 'belonging to me', and a noun for a pit dug for ore or a plentiful store of anything.

clue.text: Schmaltzy book returned by student on Scots island

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a book, read backwards here
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides
L for learner, as on a driving plate

explanation.surface: A sentimental book is brought back by a student staying on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The student is 'on' the island, so L follows IONA.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is excessive sentimentality, so a schmaltzy work is heavily emotional.

clue.text: Green sauce mostly something in gut

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: eco- denotes environmentally friendly, green
lip is cheek or impudence, as is sauce

explanation.surface: A green sauce seems mostly to be something that ends up in your stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauce here is cheeky talk, not a condiment; LIP loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a bacterium that lives naturally in the intestines.

clue.text: Sewage emptied in East River

indicators.note: an emptied word has had its contents removed, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of sewage
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Sewage has been discharged into an eastern river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seine is the river flowing through Paris.

clue.text: Repaired hash-pipes in good order

indicators.note: repaired things are put back together in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Fixed-up cannabis pipes are back in working condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means neat and tidy, as a well-run vessel should be kept.

clue.text: As a rule eat beef — ox perfect cooked with rice!

indicators.note: cooked ingredients are mixed and transformed, as these letters are

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Dietary advice: as a rule, eat beef, with ox cooked perfectly alongside rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' looks like a casual phrase introducing advice, but the answer is itself a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the well-known English spelling mnemonic, so the answer literally is a rule.

clue.text: Crabby Blair is CE? That's changed!

indicators.note: a changed set of letters has been reordered into something new

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Was Tony Blair a grumpy Church of England man? Things are different now.
explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Irascible means quick-tempered and easily annoyed, the same disposition as crabby.

clue.text: She who may exhibit power in wielding blade?

definitions.text: She who may exhibit power in wielding blade?

parts.words: She who may exhibit power in wielding blade?
parts.note: surface reading: a woman swinging a sword or knife with great strength
setter's reading: the blade is the flat end of an oar, and the power is in rowing

explanation.surface: A formidable swordswoman shows her strength with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: Blade suggests a sword, but rowers call the end of the oar its blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A female rower pulls an oar, whose flat end is the blade, putting power into each stroke.

clue.text: See 14
Use it anyhow keeping fish for religious service

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside
anyhow means in a careless, haphazard order

parts.note: the anagram fodder
the char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: Instructions to use a fish however you like for a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist is the Christian sacrament of Holy Communion, a central act of worship.

clue.text: Chap will sink putt in ghastly situation?

parts.note: he'll, short for 'he will'
to hole a putt is to sink it in golf

explanation.surface: A golfer will sink his putt in a dreadful predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A hellhole is a thoroughly unpleasant place; the question mark admits a place is stretched to a situation.

clue.text: See 14
Worry or laugh about publicity account

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the laugh goes around the other pieces

parts.note: he-he, a giggle
an ad is an advertisement
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Should one fret or laugh about the cost of advertising?
explanation.walkthrough: The laugh is a doubled 'he', the giggle sound split around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache is a source of worry or trouble, figuratively as well as literally.

clue.text: Penny met up with the French in shrine

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written and read backwards
P is the abbreviation for penny
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny met up with French friends at a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny looks like a name, but stands for P.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a building of worship, and a shrine is a sacred place of the same kind.

clue.text: Revolutionary movement in West he introduced to alliance

indicators.note: something introduced to a group is brought inside it

parts.note: a cartel is an alliance of businesses
W is the abbreviation for west
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political uprising in the West is brought into an alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary movement' suggests a political uprising, but the movement is gymnastic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartwheel is a gymnastic move where the body turns over sideways, so it literally revolves.

clue.text: Stiff and cold — that puts off female

indicators.note: to put something off here is to shed it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: frigid means very cold
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Someone stiff and cold who drives women away.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means unable to bend, which is what stiff describes.

clue.text: Directors wearied by tedious things we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: bored means wearied by dull things

explanation.surface: Company directors are worn out by tedious matters, so we're told.
explanation.definitionFit: The board is the body of directors who run a company.

clue.text: Sudden disappointment has bishop miserable

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
low means downcast

explanation.surface: A bishop is downcast after a sudden setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a shock or setback, figuratively a hit that brings disappointment.

clue.text: Time to welcome new poet

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a date is a point in time
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: It is time to greet a fresh new poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet who wrote the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Times given stick? I should say so!

parts.note: by means multiplied by, as in three by four
to gum is to stick with glue

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is time to be beaten, and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum' is a mild exclamation associated with northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: By gum is an old-fashioned exclamation of emphasis or surprise, like 'I should say so!'

clue.text: Pushing for poet Andrew?

parts.note: pro means in favour of
Andrew Motion, British Poet Laureate 1999 to 2009

explanation.surface: Campaigning on behalf of the poet Andrew Motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushing' works as a noun here: the pushing of a product.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is advertising or publicising something, the act of pushing it on buyers.

clue.text: Threatened goal with cross

parts.note: an end is an aim
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: A footballer menaced over a goal scored from a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross reads as a football pass but means angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Endangered means put at risk, as a threatened species is.

clue.text: Regularly sat by set, getting eye problem

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Someone who always sits next to the television develops an eye complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the edge of the eyelid.
